data.plain_english: US stock futures slipped as borrowing costs and oil prices rose again, and investors are waiting for notes from the US central bank. The council thinks higher borrowing costs mostly hurt property companies in the US and Hong Kong, and also Hong Kong technology firms. Most other areas look unclear, and the Shanghai market was closed for a holiday, so its reaction is still unknown. The biggest disagreement is over Chinese technology shares, which fell a lot but may bounce or fall further once trading resumes. This is research to help you think, not advice to buy or sell anything.
